title: Clean and Unclean Food, Tithes

questions.question: Since you are sons of the Lord, what should you not do for the dead?
options: Cut yourselves or make any baldness on your foreheads
questions.correctAnswer: Cut yourselves or make any baldness on your foreheads
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:1 (ESV): "You are the sons of the LORD your God. You shall not cut yourselves or make any baldness on your foreheads for the dead."

questions.question: Which land animals may execute be eaten?
options: Whatever parts the hoof and is cloven-footed and chews the cud
questions.correctAnswer: Whatever parts the hoof and is cloven-footed and chews the cud
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:6 (ESV): "Every animal that parts the hoof and has the hoof cloven in two and chews the cud... you may eat."

questions.question: Which water creatures may be eaten?
options: Anything that has fins and scales
questions.correctAnswer: Anything that has fins and scales
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:9 (ESV): "Of all that are in the waters you may eat these: whatever has fins and scales you may eat."

questions.question: What should not be boiled in its mother's milk?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:21 (ESV): "You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk."

questions.question: How often should the tithe be brought?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:22 (ESV): "You shall tithe all the yield of your seed that comes from the field year by year."

questions.question: Is the pig clean or unclean?
options: Unclean, because it parts the hoof but does not chew the cud
questions.correctAnswer: Unclean, because it parts the hoof but does not chew the cud
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:8 (ESV): "And the pig, because it parts the hoof but does not chew the cud, is unclean for you."

questions.question: What if the way to the chosen place is too long to carry the tithe?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:24–25 (ESV): "And if the way is too long for you... then you shall turn it into money..."

questions.question: What can be bought with the tithe money?
options: Whatever you desire (oxen, sheep, wine, strong drink)
questions.correctAnswer: Whatever you desire (oxen, sheep, wine, strong drink)
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:26 (ESV): "and spend the money for whatever you desire—oxen or sheep or wine or strong drink..."

questions.question: At the end of every three years, where does the tithe go?
options: Stored within your towns for the Levite, sojourner, fatherless, widow
questions.correctAnswer: Stored within your towns for the Levite, sojourner, fatherless, widow
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:28–29 (ESV): "At the end of every three years you shall bring out all the tithe... and store it within your towns."

questions.question: Which bird is NOT listed as unclean?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:12-18 lists unclean birds like eagles, owls, storks. Clean birds are not listed but are generally understood.

questions.question: May you eat anything that has died of itself?
options: No, give it to the sojourner or sell it to a foreigner
questions.correctAnswer: No, give it to the sojourner or sell it to a foreigner
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:21 (ESV): "You shall not eat anything that has died naturally. You may give it to the sojourner... or you may sell it to a foreigner..."

questions.question: Which of these is unclean?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:7 (ESV): "The camel, the hare, and the rock badger... are unclean for you."

questions.question: Why are winged insects generally unclean?
options: All winged insects are unclean for you (with exceptions in Lev, but Deut says "all")
questions.correctAnswer: All winged insects are unclean for you (with exceptions in Lev, but Deut says "all")
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:19 (ESV): "And all winged insects are unclean for you; they shall not be eaten." (Note: Leviticus gives exceptions, but Deut is general here).

questions.question: For the three-year tithe, why is it stored in towns?
options: That the Levite, sojourner, fatherless, and widow may eat and be filled
questions.correctAnswer: That the Levite, sojourner, fatherless, and widow may eat and be filled
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:29 (ESV): "And the Levite... and the sojourner, the fatherless, and the widow... shall come and eat and be filled..."

questions.question: Why are they a holy people?
options: The Lord has chosen you to be a people for his treasured possession
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord has chosen you to be a people for his treasured possession
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:2 (ESV): "For you are a people holy to the Lord... and the Lord has chosen you to be a people for his treasured possession..."

key_verse_text: For you are a people holy to the LORD your God, and the LORD has chosen you to be a people for his treasured possession, out of all the peoples who are on the face of the earth. (ESV)
